titulo: Do you lose most of your body heat through your head?
destinatario: se lo manda alguien a su amigo que se pone gorro pero sale con la campera abierta, para decirle que tape lo que queda al aire
fuentes: Vreeman RC, Carroll AE. Festive medical myths. BMJ 2008;337:a2769 (head heat loss myth; authors believe it likely originated in a military study with arctic survival suits and no hats; head is no more than about 10% of heat loss when body is exposed)

frases.texto: You were told you lose most of your body heat through your head.

frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: Heat escapes from any bare skin, roughly in proportion to how much is showing.
Your head is only about ten percent of your body's surface.
So it loses roughly ten percent of your heat at most, not half.
Doctors writing in the BMJ think the myth probably started with an old military test, where volunteers wore arctic suits but no hats.
That would explain it: their heads were the only skin showing.
Heads up: a bare head in the cold still loses heat, so a hat helps. It just isn't special.
Today, cover whatever is bare, not just your head.
Send this to the friend who wears a hat but leaves the jacket open.
